LESSON: PROJECT

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Tools and Production
Topic 4.3: Project
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 20

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Project, part of Tools and Production in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are competencies acquired in Pre-Technical Studies used to solve day- to- day problems?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to project work in the community,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify a problem in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. select an item that can be made to solve the identified problem,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. make an item to solve the problem identified using locally available materials,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. utilise skills learnt in solving problems in the day-to-day life. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print media to search for terms used in projects. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to practise how to sign and fingerspell the terms identified and list terms related to the project. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to explore the locality to establish problems that can be solved using the skills acquired in this learning area. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss the problems in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired. Ensure learners are seated in an appropriate arrangement that supports use of bi lingual communication during the discussions. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use a print or digital media to search for information on possible items to solve the identified problem, How are competencies acquired in Pre-Technical Studies used to solve day- to- day problems? 42 • In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss possible items that can be made to solve the identified problem, • In purposive groups, learners are guided to select one item that can be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem. • In pairs, learners are guided to sketch the item that can be made using the skills acquired to solve the identified problem. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use locally available materials and tools to make the identified item. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to prepare and estimate the cost to determine the price for the item. • Learners are guided to display the finished item to peer assessment or use digital devices to take photographs of the item and post on a digital portfolio.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Project in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Project together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learner develops evaluation and decision-making skills when selecting an item

that can be made using the skills acquired.

43

• Creativity and imagination: learner develops experimenting skills when selecting locally available materials and tools to

make the identified item.

• Self-Efficacy: learner acquires effective communication skills when describing the procedure followed in doing the

defined task and gives feedback during display of the finished item for evaluation.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner cares for tools and materials when making the item.

• Respect: learner appreciates diverse opinions of others as they discuss possible items that can be made to solve the

identified problem.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Environmental Education: learner protects natural resources as they use locally available materials and tools to make the

identified item.

• Financial Literacy: is enhanced as learner estimates the cost to determine the price for the item.

Link to other subjects:

Creative Arts: learner enhances knowledge on drawing during the sketching of an item that can be made using the skills

acquired in Pre-Technical Studies.

Suggested learning

• Digital resources

• Resource person

• Relevant textbooks and reference materials

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. sign terms related to project work in the community,
2. identify a problem in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired in Pre-Technical Studies,
3. select an item that can be made to solve the identified problem,
4. make an item to solve the problem identified using locally available materials,
5. utilise skills learnt in solving problems in the day-to-day life. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print media to search for terms used in projects. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to practise how to sign and fingerspell the terms identified and list terms related to the project. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to explore the locality to establish problems that can be solved using the skills acquired in this learning area. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss the problems in the locality that can be solved using the skills acquired.
